author: IGN
description:
Take a look at the 'Why Hand Drawn' Featurette for Street Fighter, the upcoming action-fighting movie based on the hit video game series distributed by Paramount Pictures. Get the rundown on how the animated flashbacks in the film were brought to life in the live-action rendition of Street Fighter, in theaters on October 16.

Set in 1993, estranged Street Fighters Ryu and Ken Masters are thrown back into combat when the mysterious Chun-Li recruits them for the next World Warrior Tournament: a brutal clash of fists, fate, and fury. But behind this battle royale lies a deadly conspiracy that forces them to face off against each other and the demons of their past. And if they don’t, it’s GAME OVER!

Street Fighter stars Noah Centineo, Andrew Koji, Callina Liang, Joe “Roman Reigns” Anoai, David Dastmalchian, Cody Rhodes, Andrew Schulz, Orville Peck, Curtis "50 Cent" Jackson, Jason Momoa, and more. The film is directed by Kitao Sakurai and produced by Mary Parent, Cale Boyter, Jason Momoa,

description: Mike Flanagan and Universal Studios just dropped the terrifying first trailer for The Exorcist: Martyrs at NYCC 2026. IGN's Tom Jorgensen sat down with Flanagan for a deep dive into how he went about picking up the torch for one of horror's most beloved franchises, and why cult-favorite The Exorcist III was the perfect jumping-off point for the story.
title: The Exorcist: Martyrs - Exclusive Trailer Breakdown with Director Mike Flanagan

author: IGN
description:
From revolutionary writer-director Mike Flanagan—revered creator of the acclaimed series The Fall of the House of Usher, Midnight Mass and The Haunting of Hill House and the groundbreaking films The Life of Chuck, Oculus, Doctor Sleep and Gerald’s Game—comes a radical new vision of the most terrifying title in the history of cinematic horror. 

Starring two-time Academy Award nominee Scarlett Johansson and rising young star Jacobi Jupe, Mike Flanagan’s The Exorcist: Martyrs is a Blumhouse Atomic Monster and Morgan Creek Entertainment production, in association with Red Room Pictures. 

Written and directed by Mike Flanagan, the film is produced by David Robinson (The Exorcist series, Dead Ringers series), three-time Academy Award nominee Jason Blum (Get Out, Black Phone films) and Mike Flanagan. The film is executive produced by Alexandra Magistro and Ryan Turek.

The Exorcist: Martyrs opens in theaters on March 12, 2027.
title: The Exorcist: Martyrs - Official Trailer (2027) Scarlett Johansson, Jacobi Jupe, Sasha Calle

author: IGN
description:
In today's Daily Fix:
Analytics firm Ampere has revealed sales numbers for Marvel's Wolverine. Roughly 35% of global sales for the game were physical disc copies, and in Europe physical sales accounted for 51% of sales. But it's probably too late for the "no disc no buy" movement as Sony has not budged from its plans to eventually stop producing phsyical game discs for first-party games. In other news, Paramount is continuing its video game adaptation momentum with a Cyberpunk 2077 movie. CD Projekt is involved, but there are no details on story, cast, or director yet.
title: 35% of Wolverine Sales Were Physical Discs - IGN Daily Fix

author: IGN
description:
When Rockstar debuted its extended look at GTA 6 on Netflix, it was as if the developer had uploaded a one-off episode of a crime thriller to the platform. 

Rockstar has always had one eye on the movies – the game that shot it to stardom is a love-letter to Goodfellas, and its most recent open-world is the greatest Western never filmed. But the cinematic ambition we associate with the studio truly came to fruition in 2004 with Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. Its predecessors, GTA 3 and Vice City, had been packed with references to classic crime cinema and voiced by genuine Hollywood talent. But that wasn’t enough for San Andreas. For this ‘90s-set Californian epic, Rockstar wanted to put you in the movies. And so it designed missions that felt like they’d been pulled from the silver screen. 

There’s no better example of this than Reuniting the Families, the penultimate chapter of San Andreas’ opening act. It’s a highly-scripted, expertly directed slice of interactive storytelling tha
title: GTA San Andreas Is Where Rockstar’s Cinematic Flair Truly Began - Art of the Level
